messages:
anya: Quick share — did a hybrid-quant bring-up for jade-embed-v1. Used per-channel int6 on most linear layers + int4 for KV cache.
anya: Baseline FP16 recall@10 (wiki holdout): 0.872
anya: Hybrid quant recall@10: 0.859  (Δ = -0.013). Cosine mean shift ~0.02. silhouette down ~0.03.
anya: Logs + short dump attached (link) — ran with the standard index (hnsw, M=16, ef=128), no PQ.

sam: nice, can you paste the exact eval command you used?
anya: Sure:

```
./run_onboard_eval --model jade-embed-v1 \
  --quant-profile "int6-perchannel:lin; int4:kv" \
  --holdout wiki_holdout_10k \
  --batch 256 --index hnsw --M 16 --ef 128 \
  --metrics recall@1,recall@5,recall@10,cosine_mean --out /tmp/jade-q-hybrid.json
```

matt: did you re-normalize after quant? sometimes L2 norm drift causes recall drops.
anya: No post-normalization. Raw outputs compared. I can re-run with L2 norm enforced.

li: also try whitening (PCA mean-subtract) — some of the cluster shift might be global bias from quant noise.

anya: Good call. I ran a quick kmeans cluster sanity — centroid cosine drift per-cluster averaged 0.018, but a few small clusters moved >0.05.

eval-bot: Summary table (wiki_holdout_10k):
- recall@1: baseline 0.741 -> quant 0.733 (Δ -0.008)
- recall@5: baseline 0.841 -> quant 0.829 (Δ -0.012)
- recall@10: baseline 0.872 -> quant 0.859 (Δ -0.013)
- cosine_mean: baseline 0.912 -> quant 0.892 (Δ -0.020)

sam: those deltas are small but visible. Do we have per-query-length breakdown? Quant tends to hurt short queries more.
anya: Yup — short queries (<=8 tokens) recall@10 Δ = -0.020, long queries (>64 tokens) Δ = -0.005.

matt: try two quick experiments:
1) int8-perchannel on linear layers (instead of int6) to see cost vs quality.
2) run whitening + L2 norm postprocess on quant outputs and compare.

li: add a run with HNSW efSearch tuned (ef=256) to check search sensitivity. Higher ef sometimes masks small embedding shifts.

anya: Plan: re-run with int8-perchannel, whitening+L2, and ef=256. Will also dump the per-cluster centroid diffs and UMAP snapshots.
anya: ETA ~ today EOD. will post updated summary.

sam: awesome. also log tokenization seed/normalization — sometimes tokenization differences sneak in when using new model variants.

anya: noted. I versioned the embed pipeline config (cfg v2026-03-20a) with tokenizer hash.

matt: if whitening recovers >0.01 recall, we should include whitening as a suggested postprocess for this quant profile.

li: +1. if not, we might hold off recommending hybrid int6 until we try per-layer mix (int6 for small weights, int8 for bigger matrices).

anya: cool. will follow up. :rocket:

sam: thanks — looping in infra if we need more GPU for runs. :thumbsup:
